New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-nz-bank-account-set-up-payment-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-nz-becs-set-up-payment-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-nz-becs-set-up-payment.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/nz-bank-account/set-up-payment`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/nz-bank-account/set-up-payment, the November 7, 2026 guide documents saving a reusable NZ BECS Direct Debit PaymentMethod before charging. Use a Stripe account, enable NZ bank account in the Dashboard for eligible dynamic payment methods, and create a server-side SetupIntent with `automatic_payment_methods[enabled]=true`. Associate either a customer-configured Accounts v2 Account using `customer_account` or a Customers v1 Customer using `customer`, and retain the identity in the later server-side PaymentIntent. The Account flow uses `configuration.customer: {}` and shows `2026-10-28.preview` on Account creation; the guide calls Accounts v2 generally available for Connect and a versioned public preview for other users (new raw lines 33-100 and new raw lines 267-297). With the SetupIntent client secret, the client Payment Element collects name, email, bank account number and DDA acceptance. Without it the merchant displays the terms and confirms acceptance separately. The guide requires mandate records promptly on Stripe’s request. `stripe.confirmSetup` with `redirect: 'if_required'` can omit a return URL for this nonredirect method, but added redirect methods need one. It can error, require a different payment method, or succeed; success attaches the saved PaymentMethod. The separate later server-side examples set `confirm=true` and `off_session=true` on an NZD PaymentIntent for either customer model. The November method overview’s Off-session payments Unsupported row leaves support unresolved despite those examples. Setup success saves the PaymentMethod. Neither the examples nor `processing` establish a completed debit (new raw lines 102-151, new raw lines 203-259 and new raw lines 267-329). The mandate email follows successful setup, and the date/amount email is due no later than each debit day; Stripe sends them by default with a custom option (new raw lines 261-265). The May capture recommended Accounts v2, but illustrated a v1 Customer and explicit `nz_bank_account`; `source-stripe-nz-becs-set-up-payment.md` lines 13-35 preserves the May path and needs both November routes and conditional setup outcomes (old raw lines 8-14, old raw lines 35-65, old raw lines 221-256 and old raw lines 258-275).
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/nz-bank-account/set-up-payment, the concrete Accounts v2 customer route, conditional Dashboard opt-in through Reusable payment methods for Global Payouts, versioned Account creation example, and switch from manually listing `nz_bank_account` to Dashboard-activated eligible dynamic methods are substantive documentation changes (old raw lines 8-14, old raw lines 51-65, new raw lines 33-100 and new raw lines 267-297). Keep the May 3 Customer/manual route and older examples dated in `source-stripe-nz-becs-set-up-payment.md`. Ruby/ERB and cURL replacing Node.js examples, Endive replacing Dahlia in the browser script, and image/table formatting are presentation changes (old raw lines 139-150 and new raw lines 153-164). Separately, both May Create examples write `payment_method_types` for `nz_bank_account` (old raw lines 51-65 and old raw lines 258-275). The changelog’s `2026-09-30.endive` REST scope rejects that write with HTTP 400 `payment_method_types_no_longer_supported` for PaymentIntent create/update/confirm and SetupIntent create/update, retaining the response property as read-only. Use Dashboard-managed dynamic methods, optionally excluding types with `excluded_payment_method_types`, or allowlist dynamically compatible types with `allowed_payment_method_types`. The changelog’s separate Impact text advises removing the field before upgrading to `2026-08-26.preview` (changelog lines 9-24, 28, 34-36). Keep both server API version references distinct from Stripe.js Endive and the `2026-10-28.preview` Accounts v2 creation example (new raw lines 49-65). In reciprocal NZ BECS references preserve the May mandate sample’s 5 business days versus the November sample’s 5 days. The May method overview already said 5 days. For the distinct debit date and amount notice, the separate deadline is no later than the day of each debit. The November method overview says Stripe’s default is to send the mandate confirmation email immediately after SetupIntent success and the debit email immediately after every successful PaymentIntent confirmation. Switching off Stripe’s emails to send custom notices requires contacting Stripe Support (old raw lines 195-212, old raw lines 250-256, new raw lines 207-224 and new raw lines 261-265, plus November method overview lines 224-249 and specifically line 228). The old tooltip incorrectly describes a PaymentIntent secret (old raw lines 68-70). November correctly identifies a SetupIntent secret in new raw lines 102-104 and new raw lines 129-133, while new raw lines 185-189 and new raw lines 233-239 still include PaymentIntent reference links. This is a reference correction with residual misleading links. The client uses the SetupIntent secret and `stripe.confirmSetup`, with `redirect: 'if_required'` and no return URL for the nonredirect NZ BECS path, and a return URL when adding a redirect-based method. The result can fail, require a different payment method or succeed (new raw lines 233-259). The November setup guide shows later PaymentIntent Create with `off_session=true` for both Accounts v2 `customer_account` and Customers v1 `customer` (new raw lines 259-297). The same-date NZ BECS method overview says Off-session payments Unsupported, even though it shows recurring payments, SetupIntents and PaymentIntents with `setup_future_usage` as Supported (overview lines 71-73 and 191-207). Preserve this unresolved conflict in both routes. Neither a saved PaymentMethod, the example request, nor a later `processing` debit establishes off-session eligibility, collection or funds availability.
